body: If this is a serious issue then we may need to revert since I won't be able to look at this for a while.

I'm not in much trouble personally.
I can use the following workaround.
```lua
vim.treesitter.get_string_parser(str, language, { injections = { [language] = "" } })
```

It seems to be specific to the string parser, since the same lua snippet is parsed correctly in a buffer. It's a bit weird since neither the Lua nor the Vim injections make use of the `offset` directive.
The change modified some of the injection stuff which is why it's broke

OK, I think I see what's going on: for a string parser, the `self._source` is the string itself rather than a number as in an actual tree, so the region adjustment here is never called:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/015656abd72b7ccac966f21218c4d7108800237a/runtime/lua/vim/treesitter/languagetree.lua#L267-L282

(Note the `TODO` right above this check ;))

So we need to add a similar correction for `type(self._source) == "string"`, e.g., using `vim.fn.byteidx()`.

Something like
```lua
function LanguageTree:set_included_regions(regions)
  -- Transform the tables from 4 element long to 6 element long (with byte offset)
  for _, region in ipairs(regions) do
    for i, range in ipairs(region) do
      if type(range) == 'table' and #range == 4 then
        local start_row, start_col, end_row, end_col = unpack(range)
        local start_byte = 0
        local end_byte = 0
        if type(self._source) == 'number' then
          -- Easy case, this is a buffer parser
          -- TODO(vigoux): proper byte computation here, and account for EOL ?
          start_byte = a.nvim_buf_get_offset(self._source, start_row) + start_col
          end_byte = a.nvim_buf_get_offset(self._source, end_row) + end_col
        elseif type(self._source) == 'string' then
          -- string parser, single `\n` delimited string
          start_byte = vim.fn.byteidx(self._source, start_col)
          end_byte = vim.fn.byteidx(self._source, end_col)
        end

        region[i] = { start_row, start_col, start_byte, end_row, end_col, end_byte }
      end
    end
  end

  self._regions = regions
  -- Trees are no longer valid now that we have changed regions.
  -- TODO(vigoux,steelsojka): Look into doing this smarter so we can use some of the
  --                          old trees for incremental parsing. Currently, this only
  --                          effects injected languages.
  self._trees = {}
  self:invalidate()
end
```
seems to work. @notomo could you test that?

@clason 
Thanks!
I confirmed that the change fixed this issue.

📝 To confirm, I replaced the following lines, rebuilt nvim and execute minimal.lua.
